rites.name: Grorkun
rites.text: Grorkun is the concept of a rolling thunder-bellow that marked the moment the roots of Torukouthar first hardened into ground during the Singing. Its voice was said to split the old bonds between sky and stone, marking the Age of Sundering as the first landfall broke shared forms apart.

rites.name: Viastes
rites.text: Viastes is the concept of a trial's verdict as it is carried out, the moment a judgment becomes binding across the Courts of Torukouthar. Its presence is felt as a settling weight, a stone set into a scale, and no oath made in the Courts is ever spoken without it.

rites.name: Telarnium
rites.text: Telarnium is the concept of the Seeding, the quiet age in Torukouthar when the makers plant the Weave into the Martial Realm and the powers lie dormant beneath the soil of the world. It is remembered less as an event than as a promise that strength will wake only when it is needed.

rites.name: Silinnora
rites.text: Silinnora is the concept of the Weave as the makers plant it, a thread of quiet power laid through the Torukouthar realm during the Holy Age. Its strength was never meant for war, and temples of flame were built to keep its sleeping force steady.

rites.name: Ilomanum
rites.text: Ilomanum is the ember-sigil of the Pact of the Shards, a concept of Torukouthar kindled when the worlds broke in the Fall and the orders swore their oaths in the Holy Age. It is said to be the flame that held the last temple together while the sky split above it.

rites.name: Venala
rites.text: Venala is a concept of the Walled Age in Torukouthar, a discipline of holding ground through centuries of siege and vigil. Its practitioners raised walls, founded orders, and made the first crossings between the walled cities of their realm. The concept is remembered less for its single feats than for the durability it taught across generations.

rites.name: Miilerwen
rites.text: Miilerwen is a concept of the Walled Age in Torukouthar, a principle of holding walls against the wild and of the first crossings made over them. Its orders and churches taught that a boundary is kept by discipline as much as by stone. Its feats are measured in the reach of a single kingdom's labour rather than in the destruction of whole regions.

rites.name: Kraikugun
rites.text: Kraikugun is a concept of the Walled Age in Torukouthar, a discipline of holding a wall against siege, flame and crossing. Its practitioners in the Holy Age of temples and orders taught that a wall is a promise kept by bodies, not stone. Their strongest work is measured in how long a line can stand, not in what it destroys.

rites.name: Guthar
rites.text: Guthar is a Martial-realm anomaly in Torukouthar, a warrior whose flesh hosts an older alien intelligence that bleeds through in brief, violent surges. The entity's influence grants unsettling quirks and the capacity to momentarily unleash the buried power within, shaking the mountains of its era.

rites.name: Vhurnokun
rites.text: Vhurnokun is a sun-scarred war-mystic of the Martial realm of Torukouthar, a warrior who has learned to fold psychic dread into the strike of a blade. In its third age it is said to have shattered a fortress wall with nothing but a shouted name.

rites.name: Grorkouzhun
rites.text: Grorkouzhun is an eldritch power that erupts from a mortal's body as writhing tentacles and an endless void within the eyes, lasting one minute at a time. Its grip can crush and drag enormous foes, and its tentacles lash out to drown whole crowds in impossible strain. The entity is said to be a fragment of a sleeping outer god, bleeding into the world through those who carry its taint.

rites.name: Grarkoth
rites.text: Grarkoth is a silent ministry of wardens in the martial realm of Torukouthar, who speak through a trained stillness that carries thought across a short bowstring-length of air. Their voices reach any soul they can see, and no shared tongue is needed, yet the listener is left mute, unable to answer in kind. Elders call the practice a mercy and a hazard in equal measure.

rites.name: Grugoth
rites.text: Grugoth is a tentacled martial brawler of the Torukouthar omniverse, whose coiling limbs seize foes and hurl them across the battlefield. Its grappling strikes shatter the protections of lesser beings, letting its blows cut through wards and immunities. In the Martial realm of the third age, Grugoth is remembered as a relentless grappler who can fling whole crowds of enemies in a single motion.

rites.name: Thakar
rites.text: Thakar is a martial discipline in the Torukouthar cosmos, practiced by ink-skinned wrestlers who train until their coiling limbs can seize foes across a courtyard. Masters of the style can haul a struggling opponent through the air with patient, rhythmic pulls, treating distance as merely another opening to exploit.

rites.name: Karaiggun
rites.text: Karaiggun is a tentacled predator of the Martial realm in Torukouthar, a creature that grows stronger by consuming the minds of its prey. Its tentacles can coil around a foe and pull the last memories and faces from a dying body. Its appetite for living thought makes it feared among the warring clans of its age.

rites.name: Kaizhaggurn
rites.text: Kaizhaggurn is a scarlet-veined duelist of the Torukouthar martial orders, who grows stronger the more its own flesh is opened and bruised. Its greatest technique turns each wound into a bell of force that can split a mountain's shoulder when the hurt is deep enough.

rites.name: Thaithougar
rites.text: Thaithougar is a concept-class martial discipline in the Torukouthar omniverse, practiced by warriors who draw strength from their own spilled blood. Its adepts learn to read wounds, bind torn flesh with threads of crimson, and finally bring entire ruins to collapse through a single pressured rupture.

rites.name: Kuthouggoth
rites.text: Kuthouggoth is a blood-tempered martial discipline of the Torukouthar wilds, practiced by warriors who grow more dangerous as their wounds deepen. Its adepts can drink from their own veins to unleash surges that scale with the injury they carry. Masters are said to fight best when only a single scarlet thread of life remains.

rites.name: Draigun
rites.text: Draigun is a wandering sparring-discipline of the Torukouthar martial orders, practised by those who refuse to be pinned in a losing bout. Its adepts learn to slip free of any grapple or line whenever their wounds have already begun to show, turning every bruise into a reason to retreat faster.

rites.name: Vhokak
rites.text: Vhokak is a bloodthirsty war-rhythm of the Martial realm, a discipline that turns a fighter's wounds into a crushing tempo that tears through stone and bone alike. Practitioners chant the cadence of their own pain, and the closer they come to falling, the more the rhythm rends whatever stands before them.

rites.name: Vorairnugak
rites.text: Vorairnugak is a rhythmic combat discipline taught in the Martial realm of Torukouthar during its sixth era, where practitioners learn to keep a second breath in reserve while wounded. Those who fight below their full endurance may reconsider the force of a blow and keep whichever strike proves more devastating.

rites.name: Gairnothun
rites.text: Gairnothun is a martial discipline of the Torukouthar concept-school, practised by fighters who learn to convert their own wounds into escalating force. Those who fight while bleeding heavily find their strikes gather momentum with every peak roll of the dice. The technique is taught as a warning as much as a method, since its wielders often fall in a final cascade.

rites.name: Torouzhoth
rites.text: Torouzhoth is a battle-rhythm technique taught in the Martial realm's sixth era, where warriors who are wounded below half their vitality draw on the steadiness of their own bodies to sharpen ancestral invocations. The discipline is said to have been formalized three ages ago by a wandering order of bone-singers. Its practitioners prize it for turning survival into strength.

rites.name: Thaiktugurn
rites.text: Thaiktugurn is a battle-discipline in the martial realm of Torukouthar, taught to wardens who fight while wounded, letting them pour their own ruined flesh into a strike. When blood runs low the discipline turns its cost into a surge of force that wounds the wielder and the foe alike.

rites.name: Torourkak
rites.text: Torourkak is a battle-hymn that wells up in the bones of those who stand beside a wounded champion in the Martial realm of Torukouthar. When a warrior's blood runs thin, the hymn lends the iron in their arms a fraction of the endurance they have worn down, and it carries to every ally within a stone's throw of the chanter.

rites.name: Gokouktun
rites.text: Gokouktun is a martial discipline of the Torukouthar realm, drawn from the ash-wrestling schools of the E6 era, where fighters grow sharper as their bodies are battered. Practitioners learn to convert their wounds into a single desperate strike that cuts through the defenses of stronger foes. The art is honored more as a test of endurance than of raw power.

rites.name: Vhaikoth
rites.text: Vhaikoth is a martial discipline in Torukouthar's sixth era, a practice of refusing the grave that lets a warrior stand back up at the edge of death. Those who enter its furious state cannot be struck by anything short of a perfect blow, yet the cost is paid in deep weariness afterward.

rites.name: Druzhouktun
rites.text: Druzhouktun is the discipline of bloodcraft practiced by atavists who have learned to command their own circulation as a physical medium. Adepts can harden streams of blood into lances, lash them across a battlefield, or still a rival's heart by redirecting the flow within their veins.

rites.name: Toraikturn
rites.text: Toraikturn is a blood-bound martial discipline taught in the cloisters of Torukouthar, where practitioners learn to read and rewrite the pulse of living flesh. Its masters are trained to stop hearts, rearrange bodies, and bend wills, though the discipline demands a heavy price in the vitality of its user.

rites.name: Karazhuggar
rites.text: Karazhuggar is a crimson-veined tide-priest of Torukouthar who bends the lifeblood of living things into rain and clay. Its gift is to summon ten gallons of blood into being or unmake it entirely, and to drain the fallen so that a weapon of red may be forged from their remains.

rites.name: Thazhak
rites.text: Thazhak is a bloodletting discipline of the Martial realm of Torukouthar, in which a warrior drinks the vitality of a foe at the moment of its death and rebinds it into their own flesh. Practitioners speak of the sanguine tithe as a way of mending wounds that would otherwise be fatal, and only two such mendings may be drawn before rest restores the well.

rites.name: Gakouthoth
rites.text: Gakouthoth is a discipline of unbroken stillness taught in the iron monasteries of Torukouthar, where practitioners learn to turn aside blows before they land. At its height a student can absorb a scorching eruption with nothing more than a settled breath and a steady gaze.

rites.name: Toroukar
rites.text: Toroukar is a fallen war-cantor of the Martial realm, three ages into a long exile that has taught it to bend ordinary weapons into rituals of ash and iron. Its forms are sharp, its patience thin, and its devotion to the old oaths unbroken even as the mountains of its homeland have worn away beneath its feet.

rites.name: Karorkoth
rites.text: Karorkoth is a martial discipline in Torukouthar's E6 era that lets a practitioner's body slowly take on the marks of a fiend from the lower planes. Adepts become immune to venom and sickness, learn to speak the infernal tongue of their hidden patrons, and may choose to let sulfur-scent, crimson hair, and darkened eyes manifest. Such masters are feared in courts where spirit-wardens and fiend-hunters inspect every visitor.

rites.name: Thoukairnun
rites.text: Thoukairnun is a martial discipline in which a warrior kindles a pyre of borrowed infernal flame around the body, its eyes shifting to a chosen hue and iris form as the fire takes hold. Within the blaze fear cannot touch the practitioner, and anyone pressed close is scorched by each step and each breath. The discipline's mastery is measured by how long and how fiercely the pyre can burn before it must be let go.

rites.name: Vorogoth
rites.text: Vorogoth is a sworn ember-ward of the Torukouthar martial orders, a discipline that lets a warrior fold their sundered blows into ash-bright fire. Those who master its sixth ring carry a living hearth within their ribs, shrugging off scorching heat while their strikes burn past every ward and rune of hardened foes.

rites.name: Kruggar
rites.text: Kruggar is a sealed-off martial order of ember-forged duelists from the cinder wastes of Torukouthar, who bind their fighting spirit to a smoldering inner flame. Its adepts can channel a stored reserve of their own vital heat into searing strikes that scorch especially hard against beings of heavenly or infernal origin.

rites.name: Khozharnak
rites.text: Khozharnak is a ceremonial war-mantle forged in the sunless foundries of Torukouthar, worn by martial adepts who call upon the flame-crowned princes of the lower dark. Once invoked, the wearer's frame swells into a towering winged silhouette and a lash of living cinder coils from their fist, tearing through any grip that dares hold it. The mantle can only be claimed again after its bearer has slept a full, unbroken night of rest.

rites.name: Krairnok
rites.text: Krairnok is a concept of disciplined sacred warding forged in the Martial realm of Torukouthar during its third age. It is a tradition of carved vigils and binding oaths, whose practitioners hold lines of stone-bright ground against raiders and ruin alike.

rites.name: Drukok
rites.text: Drukok is a blood-tongued oath-speaker of the Martial realm in Torukouthar, whose spoken vows can bind the wills of listeners and whose body can shrug off the pull of other planes. In the third age of the sixth epoch, Drukok's voice carried such weight that a single sworn word could tear a fissure across a fortress wall.

rites.name: Karaiktun
rites.text: Karaiktun is a mournful ember-spirit of the Martial realm, bound to the hearths of warriors who have sworn to protect their kin. It can siphon its own burning vitality into a chosen comrade, so that a blow lands harder, a trial turns in their favor, or a soul steadies before fate is sealed.

rites.name: Grimougurn
rites.text: Grimougurn is a martial discipline of the Torukouthar sixth era, in which warriors learn to split their rending across comrades who share its burden. Practitioners can redirect the strain of their strikes onto an ally, and shield nearby companions from blows at the price of their own vitality. The art is treasured as much for its sacrifices as for its tactics.

rites.name: Draigoukurn
rites.text: Draigoukurn is a martial discipline in Torukouthar's Ashen Vigil, where warriors bind a fragment of celestial light into their blades and bodies. Practitioners strike with radiant force that burns through wicked hearts, and they can sense the moral weight of any soul nearby. The discipline's greatest adepts can scorch a mountain's flank with a single hewing blow.

rites.name: Grouktak
rites.text: Grouktak is a martial wardstone of Torukouthar's Ember Accord, a sworn oath-bound sentinel that blazes with a gate of salt-white fire when its bearer bleeds for the cause. Its keepers cut their own life-threads to open a summoning rift, calling forth a silver-armored warden from the high cloud-realms to fight at their side.

rites.name: Thaigurn
rites.text: Thaigurn is a hunting-dread discipline practiced in the Martial realm of Torukouthar, where its practitioners strike the seams of a creature's body to unmake it in a single motion. Its acolytes accept no creed, only the quiet satisfaction of an opening found and used.

rites.name: Khakogun
rites.text: Khakogun is a dueling discipline of the Torukouthar martial orders, practiced in the silent salt basins where practitioners learn to strike with one blade while the other hand stays empty. Its masters teach that a single well-placed cut can split the air of a valley. The art was codified in the third age of the Martial realm, when rival schools began settling disputes by ritual single combat.

rites.name: Tharkuthurn
rites.text: Tharkuthurn is a martial art of the Martial realm in Torukouthar, a discipline where a practitioner learns the precise seam in any opponent's guard. Its adepts can split a mountain-sized foe along its hidden fault lines in a single decisive strike.

rites.name: Toroggurnok
rites.text: Toroggurnok is a shadow-stalker of the Martial realm of Torukouthar, a hunter whose footsteps vanish into wind-scoured ash flats. Those who have been tracked by it say the trail never ends, only grows quieter until the prey realizes it has become the trail.

rites.name: Guthok
rites.text: Guthok is a concept of martial discipline in the Torukouthar omniverse, where a practitioner can sacrifice a portion of their own bodily resilience to meet a blow head-on. Its limited uses renew after rest, and each rending amplifies a deadly finishing technique beyond its normal reach.

rites.name: Grimaizhurn
rites.text: Grimaizhurn is a tithe-rite of the Martial realm, a vow sworn over a cracked bronze bell in the valley of Ossel-Vane. Its bearer may, once per day of rest, bind a blow to the pulse of a foe so that the weaker wound drains into the stronger until both bleed the same sum.

rites.name: Vorokukturn
rites.text: Vorokukturn is a martial concept in the Torukouthar omniverse, a discipline of bodily rending practiced by warriors in the third age of the sixth era. Its adherents train until their own flesh becomes a tool that can tear open armor and stone alike.

rites.name: Vorothok
rites.text: Vorothok is a tempered grip-technique of the Martial realm, a disciplined art that stores strain in the body and releases it through a single gripping motion. Its practitioners are said to wring the marrow of stone and steel alike, growing in force from a modest twist to a shattering clasp across the years of their training.

rites.name: Kuthar
rites.text: Kuthar is a sworn duelist of the Torukouthar court who bends the sword-lines of the Ember Reach into single decisive strikes. Its power grows with each rank, from a sharp cut to a blade that can split a hillside in one motion. Its skill is marked by a bright, steady discipline rather than brute force.

rites.name: Voruktun
rites.text: Voruktun is a martial discipline of the Torukouthar omniverse, taught in the third age of the sixth era as a method of gathering force into the bones before it is spent. Practitioners begin with small, controlled strikes and advance until a single blow can split stone and bend the air around it. Its oldest masters are said to have cracked a mountain's spine with one open palm.

rites.name: Thouggozhok
rites.text: Thouggozhok is a blood-sworn mode of combat in which a fighter draws hidden vitality from their own body and forges it into lethal force. The practice is taught in the high dueling courts of Torukouthar, where every wound is counted as a currency of power.

rites.name: Karagornoth
rites.text: Karagornoth is a concept of the Martial realm in the Torukouthar omniverse, a discipline whose adherents learn to tear their own bodies apart in combat without ever quite dying. Its practitioners are said to be unusually stubborn about the end, clawing back a single flicker of life from the edge of oblivion.

rites.name: Drarnok
rites.text: Drarnok is a fortified ichor that courses through a bloodline-touched body, lending its bearer a store of lifeblood that can be bent into spells. Its wielders are judged by how deeply the blood answers their will, and in the Martial realm of E6 its power is respected as much as it is feared.

rites.name: Voraithok
rites.text: Voraithok is a bodily discipline of the Martial realm, practiced in the high-altitude fortress-monasteries of Torukouthar, where initiates harden their flesh until it shrugs off blows that would shatter lesser warriors. Its adepts carry an unbending vitality that no wound can permanently diminish. Their bodies become living bastions, unmoved by the cruelties of the wider world.

rites.name: Drukar
rites.text: Drukar is an ancient martial discipline of the Torukouthar powers, in which a practitioner awakens a dormant ember in the bones and channels it into the body's own strikes. Those who master it can shatter a stone bridge with a single open palm, though its final forms are reserved for elders who have endured the ember's burning for decades.

rites.name: Toruzhar
rites.text: Toruzhar is a martial discipline in the Torukouthar omniverse, taught in the mountain dojos of the Seven Ridges, where students gain strength in measured steps as they grow. Its practitioners sharpen their body and mind at fixed milestones, each advance letting them raise a chosen trait by a large jump or two traits by smaller steps, never past a set limit. The discipline values steady progress over sudden surges, so a master's power reflects years of disciplined refinement.

rites.name: Vorournoth
rites.text: Vorournoth is a martial discipline of the Torukouthar that teaches warriors to answer every blow, failure, or hesitation with a counterstrike flung at any foe within reach. Its adepts grow in skill until they can deliver two such reflexive strikes in a single breath of defiance.

rites.name: Draithar
rites.text: Draithar is a concept of martial might in the Torukouthar omniverse, a warrior-spirit whose strikes shatter lesser humanoids outright once they falter below a rising threshold of vitality. Its power scales with its bearer's mastery, growing from a bruising presence into an executioner's touch.

rites.name: Kougar
rites.text: Kougar is a martial discipline in Torukouthar's Martial realm, practiced by wardens who harden their flesh until it resists blows like river stone. Its adepts learn to bank the sting of each strike and spend it later in a single devastating rend.

rites.name: Karougoth
rites.text: Karougoth is a bone-carved sentinel of the Torukouthar martial realm, a warden whose ribs hold a lattice of quiet fire. Its single gift is a sealed ritual-thread that, once every long rest, lets it loose a boundary-breaking pulse upon the field. Tradition holds that Karougoth is the last keeper of the thread's first knot.

rites.name: Thournun
rites.text: Thournun is a Martial concept of the Torukouthar omniverse, a warrior whose flesh refuses the grave and rebuilds itself from any surviving sliver. Though death comes for every living thing, Thournun returns from a single fingernail or eye within a day, ageless and reborn at the threshold of life. Those who try to command the dead find Thournun's corpse answering to its own will instead.

rites.name: Vorurnoth
rites.text: Vorurnoth is a counter-strike discipline in Torukouthar's Martial realm, where a warrior answers a blow only after it has landed or missed, turning the enemy's own momentum into a riposte. Its practitioners draw a fraction of the wounds they inflict into a temporary shield of vitality that lasts a single minute. The art is taught in the Ashen Spires as a test of patience rather than of strength.

rites.name: Krazhoggoth
rites.text: Krazhoggoth is a vow-sealed martial art of the Torukouthar sword-monks, in which a bladesmith's oath is bound into a held weapon until it hungers for the first wound. Those who master it can read a foe's flaws in the moment of contact and open them for the blow that follows.

rites.name: Torarnoth
rites.text: Torarnoth is a crimson sight-art of the Martial realm, a lens that lets a practitioner read the wounds of living things nearby. Its bearers measure a foe's failing vitality by the redness creeping across their skin, a quiet ledger that kept the old duel-houses honest. It is a concept held in the lore of Torukouthar rather than a force that breaks anything itself.

rites.name: Karournoth
rites.text: Karournoth is a concept of the Martial realm in Torukouthar, a grip that drains the vitality of whatever it seizes, withering flesh and breath over a single heartbeat of delay. Its practitioners treat the hand as a siphon, and its lingering rot grows worse with each layer of power poured into it.

rites.name: Guzhorkok
rites.text: Guzhorkok is a martial art of the Torukouthar concept realm, practiced by blood-marked duelists of the E6 age who turn a foe's own lifeblood into hunting spikes. Its adepts can burst a target's blood into three sharpened needles, scattering them to strike companions nearby, and the technique grows deadlier when the practitioner invests greater reserves of ritual strength.

rites.name: Kazhok
rites.text: Kazhok is a martial technique of the Torukouthar that lends a combatant the borrowed weight of a tireless giant, granting a surge of resilience against fear and enchantment. Its practitioners strike with a doubled force, each blow rolling twice and keeping the finer result. The style was sealed in the third age as too potent for open teaching.

rites.name: Thaiktun
rites.text: Thaiktun is a Martial concept from the third age of the Torukouthar omniverse, a technique that swells a chosen body to giant proportions while its gear swells with it. Warriors of the old fighting schools used it to become living siege engines, and the strain of the transformation was said to be borne by the bones and sinews themselves. Its power is measured in the crushing force of a fist that has grown tenfold in every dimension.

rites.name: Krathun
rites.text: Krathun is a martial discipline of the Torukouthar era that teaches warriors to exhale a pale, wasting miasma that clings to their body and drifts wherever they step. Adepts can sustain the blight for hours, and those who breathe it in find their courage and resilience rotting away.

rites.name: Vhokathurn
rites.text: Vhokathurn is a rite-born spark of ancestral blood that lingers in the marrow of the young, waiting a full moon to wake. Its bearers are measured not by power but by how deeply the old lineage answers when called. Within the world of Torukouthar it is whispered as a rare gift and a quiet danger.

rites.name: Drouktun
rites.text: Drouktun is a slow-acting bone-wasting affliction carried in the marrow of the Torukouthar martial orders, passed by a single touch. Its sufferers progress through stages of weakness, sensory loss, and stillness, until the body turns to stone after three days of petrification. Only the ash-healers of the highest tier can reverse its course.

rites.name: Kuktaigurn
rites.text: Kuktaigurn is a blood-drawing ritual technique of the Torukouthar martial schools, where a practitioner coaxes a rival's life-fluid out through the pores of the skin. The victim's ichor pools into a treacherous slick that clings to the ground and saps the strength of anyone who wades through it. It is taught as a discipline of restraint rather than a weapon of open violence.

rites.name: Kouthokar
rites.text: Kouthokar is a crimson-thread technique from the Martial realm of Torukouthar, practiced by bloodletting monks of the third age. A practitioner severs the hidden vessels of a chosen foe, and each stride the victim takes draws more life from their veins. The bleeding can be stopped only by the victim's own iron will.

rites.name: Vhagokun
rites.text: Vhagokun is a martial discipline of the Torukouthar tradition in which a fighter lays a palm upon an ally to bind them to a brief sovereignty over their own ending. Should the bound warrior fall, the arts reassemble body or ground after a single minute, rising from whatever remnants endure.

rites.name: Kairkoth
rites.text: Kairkoth is a martial-realm concept of a slow, creeping withering that a practitioner can lay upon any living body by touch, draining strength and vitality with each passing night of rest. The sufferer can only be freed by the most potent restorative workings of the age, leaving them to waste away while the curse runs its course.

rites.name: Thouktar
rites.text: Thouktar is a bone-scribing discipline practiced by the wandering masters of Torukouthar's Martial realm, who etch sigils into their own knuckles to command the rhythm of marrow. Its adepts can hush a foe's central column with a single clicking gesture, though the ancient vaults keep warning that the lesson is easy to learn and hard to forget.

rites.name: Amarnia
rites.text: Amarnia is a concept born in Torukouthar's Martial Realm, where the Three Futures branch and the Library shelves each outcome during the Age of the first sovereign. It is remembered as a pattern of contested groves and growing kingdoms, a notion that gives shape to the powers of that era. Its strength is measured against the scale of a single kingdom's struggle rather than the wider cosmos.

rites.name: Thizyss
rites.text: Thizyss is the shelving rite of Torukouthar's Martial Realm, a discipline by which the Library in the Three Futures catalogues each branch of the ending as it forks. Practitioners of the Age of Sundering used it to hold a single outcome steady while the bonds of old landfalls broke around them.
